market_mood: Risk is split: oil is at a five-month high on Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and Gulf tension, while AI/data-center names keep cracking after a disastrous Korean AI IPO and Gartner's warning that neocloud returns don't justify the capex. Deal flow stays heavy (Salesforce-Braze, Tradeweb-Trumid, Labcorp-Myriad, KMB-Kenvue clearing China).
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been the weakest part of the record (2 of 10), mostly from chasing oil names after they had already run, while geopolitics and merger ideas have worked best. So today I kept sizing modest, leaned on defense and deal-driven ideas, and used oil exposure through a producer rather than refiners.

picks.reason: Braze jumped over 50% to near the $47.50 all-cash Salesforce offer, so upside is now capped and any wobble in deal expectations only moves it one way.
Labcorp is buying Myriad's prenatal testing business for $210M, a small bolt-on in a health care sector that has been the market's strongest group this past week.
Brent hit a five-month high on attacks on Saudi energy sites and shipping, and the US strategic reserve is at its lowest since 1982 — leaving little cushion if supply is disrupted further.
Gartner says 80% of neocloud firms may not survive and a Korean AI infrastructure IPO fell 30% on debut; funding costs for this group are rising fast.

Britain flying defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks and Egypt weighing military support all point to more missile-defense and munitions demand, and Northrop/RTX just raised guidance on rearmament.
Tradeweb is buying Trumid for $1.97B, extending its grip on electronic bond trading at a time of heavy rate-driven volume.

top_buys.pitch: Brent at a five-month high with the US emergency reserve at its thinnest since 1982.
top_buys.why: Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi energy and airport sites have pushed Brent to a five-month high, and Gulf markets fell on the news. The SPR being at its lowest level since 1982 means Washington has little ability to cap prices if supply is actually hit. A US producer like Occidental sees the full benefit of higher realized crude prices without refining-margin drag, which has burned my recent refiner picks.
top_buys.risks: Geopolitical premiums fade quickly if attacks stop, and energy was the weakest sector last week, so this fights a mild downtrend.
top_buys.watch: Any further Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities and the Egypt vote on military support set for October 26.

top_buys.pitch: Missile-defense demand is being underlined daily by Gulf escalation and peer guidance raises.
top_buys.why: Britain is flying defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia, Houthis are hitting Saudi energy sites, and Egypt is voting on military support — all pointing to heavier use and restocking of air and missile defense. Northrop and RTX both just raised annual profit forecasts on rearmament, which usually reads across to Lockheed. Lockheed has lagged peers, so the rearmament theme may be less priced in here.
top_buys.risks: Lockheed has program-specific execution problems that can overwhelm sector tailwinds, and a sudden de-escalation would deflate the theme.
top_buys.watch: Lockheed's own quarterly results and whether it raises guidance like its peers did.

top_buys.pitch: The neocloud funding window is closing and Gartner says most of these firms won't survive.
top_buys.why: A Korean AI infrastructure IPO fell more than 30% on debut, signalling that investors no longer want to fund this build-out at any price. Gartner's forecaster doubled down that AI returns don't justify neocloud capex and that 80% of these firms face extinction by 2030. With CoreWeave reportedly paying as much as 13% on new debt, the whole group's economics get worse as borrowing costs rise.
top_buys.risks: A big Anthropic- or hyperscaler-style contract announcement can send these stocks up 20% in a day, and the group is already heavily shorted and oversold.
top_buys.watch: Any new neocloud financing terms or a fresh multibillion-dollar AI compute contract like the rumoured Anthropic-Nscale deal.

top_buys.pitch: Cheap bolt-on in prenatal testing, in the market's hottest sector.
top_buys.why: Labcorp is acquiring Myriad Genetics' prenatal health testing business for $210 million, adding volume to an existing lab network where incremental tests carry high margins. Health care was the best-performing sector last week, up almost 6%, so the tide is in its favour. Deal-driven acquirer ideas have been my better-performing category.
top_buys.risks: The deal is small relative to Labcorp's size, so it may barely move the stock, and lab reimbursement pressure is an ongoing drag.
top_buys.watch: Labcorp's upcoming quarterly results and guidance for base business volume growth.

top_buys.pitch: Nearly $2B Trumid buy deepens Tradeweb's hold on electronic credit trading.
top_buys.why: Tradeweb is acquiring Trumid for $1.97 billion, adding a strong corporate-bond trading venue to its platform and expanding its bond lifecycle offering. Rate uncertainty — with BofA still calling for an October Fed hike against market odds — tends to drive heavy bond trading volumes, which is how Tradeweb earns. Acquirer stocks often dip on deal day and recover as the strategic logic sinks in.
top_buys.risks: Investors may balk at the price and dilution, and integration of a competitor platform carries client-attrition risk.
top_buys.watch: The Fed's October decision and Tradeweb's monthly volume disclosures.
